historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Cholinesterase inhibitors

starting.description: An early branch developed from the observed pupil-constricting effect of Calabar bean extract; the bean later supplied the cholinesterase-inhibiting alkaloid physostigmine. In the distinct donepezil branch, observed cholinergic deficits in Alzheimer brain and experience with existing inhibitors motivated a search for improved treatment; an unexpectedly active synthetic N-benzylpiperazine encountered in screening became the immediate chemical seed.

inspiration.description: Early ophthalmic investigation developed from the effects of a natural Calabar bean extract. Alzheimer cholinergic deficits and prior clinical inhibitor experience informed the later donepezil strategy; an observed effect of a synthetic piperazine compound supplied its immediate chemical seed.

steps.description: After observing the pupil-constricting effects of Calabar bean extract, Fraser and Robertson investigated its ocular actions and Robertson proposed ophthalmic uses.
The bean supplied the alkaloid physostigmine, later identified as a cholinesterase inhibitor; related inhibitors were subsequently developed.
For the later Alzheimer program, disease-associated cholinergic deficits and experience with earlier inhibitors supplied the treatment rationale.
A screened N-benzylpiperazine compound showed acetylcholinesterase inhibition and was selected as a seed.
Piperidine substitution and subsequent medicinal chemistry yielded potent derivatives; an indanone series led to donepezil, whose longer-lasting inhibition was tested against physostigmine in rats.

design.description: Early investigators studied bean extract and proposed ocular uses; later analogues modified the physostigmine lead. The donepezil developers screened and selected a separate synthetic seed, changed the piperazine to piperidine, studied structure–activity relations and designed indanone derivatives to improve activity and duration.

circumstances.description: The inhibitor program and follow-on synthesis were deliberate; encountering the chemical seed during screening was described as a chance finding by the developers.

limits: The Calabar bean/physostigmine and donepezil histories are distinct branches of a mechanism class; a shared inhibition mechanism does not prove shared molecular ancestry.
The 1863 report describes a crude extract and proposed applications, not purified physostigmine, an established enzyme mechanism, or demonstrated patient benefit.
The cohort contains donepezil alone; this record does not establish origins of every later inhibitor architecture.
conflicts: Houghton et al. 2006 (S3, E8) give 1926 for recognition of physostigmine's cholinesterase inhibition; Karczmar 2009 (S4, E9) gives 1930. The underlying original papers were not read and a possible difference in the experimental milestones is not resolved.

Houghton et al. 2006 (S3, E8) date physostigmine's isolation to 1864; Pauling and Petcher 1973 (S6, E11) say 1878. The underlying isolation publications were not read and the priority or date discrepancy is not resolved.
gaps: The nineteenth-century isolation reports and 1920s–1930s original mechanism papers were not read; the exact isolation and mechanism-discovery dates remain unresolved.

Bowen et al.'s 1976 original Alzheimer's biochemical report was read only at abstract extent; Davies and Maloney 1976 and original trials of earlier inhibitors were not read. The clinical and disease rationale therefore rests on the explicitly identified retrospective and original medicinal-chemistry introduction.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: Calabar bean self-eye testing produced pupil constriction and accommodation changes that suggested ophthalmic use.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: The later donepezil branch also relies on human postmortem biochemical assays, which do not qualify here.
